Order 
This appeal has been preferred by the appellants/claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, arising out of the award dated 25.01.2010 passed by the Member, MACT,
District Vidisha (hereinafter referred to as "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No. 41/2009.
The appeal has been filed on the grounds of inadequacy of compensation and also being aggrieved by the exoneration of the insurance company from liability.

2. The date of accident and negligence are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in question.
3.

As per findings of the Claims Tribunal, for the case of death of Masum NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:396 2 MA-629-2010 Khan, an amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.3,08,000/- has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal with interest from filing of claim petition till its realization.

4. The appellants/claimants have preferred this appeal contending that at the time of the accident,
the owner of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid permit and the driver, though holding a Salim Khan vs Smt.Jagjeet Kaur Bagga on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76064929/
1 licence for a transport vehicle, did not possess the requisite endorsement to drive a vehicle carrying hazardous goods.

entities.text: Salim Khan vs Smt.Jagjeet Kaur Bagga
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Despite this, the Claims Tribunal exonerated the insurance company from its liability.
It is further submitted that the deceased was a third party and, therefore, the insurance company is liable to pay compensation to the claimants.
Hence, the impugned award deserves modification.
5. It is further contended that the Claims Tribunal committed a grave error in assessing the income of the deceased on the lower side.
At the time of the accident, the deceased was an unskilled labourer and, as per the Minimum Wages Act, an unskilled labourer was earning Rs.3,295/- per month.

Learned counsel for the appellants further submitted that the Claims Tribunal erred in not granting future prospects and failed to award reasonable amounts under conventional heads such as loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses.
Therefore, enhancement of compensation has been prayed for.

6. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.1 & respondent No.3/Insurance Company supported the impugned Award and submitted that the Claims Tribunal has rightly assessed the compensation on the basis of the evidence available on record.

It is contended that the appeal lacks merit and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:396 3 MA-629-2010 deserves to be dismissed.
7. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
8.
Upon perusal of the record, it is found that at the time of the accident, the owner of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid route permit.
It is also found that the driver was driving a transport vehicle carrying hazardous goods, but his driving licence did not contain the required endorsement authorizing him to drive such a vehicle.
Thus, there was a clear breach of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy by both the owner and the driver.
9. It is undisputed that the deceased was a third party.

In view of the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Amrit Paul Singh vs. TATA AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd., 2019 (2) MPLJ (SC)
8, and National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Challa Bharathamma and others, 2004 ACJ 2094, even if the offending vehicle is operated without a valid and effective permit, the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation to the claimant in the first instance and thereafter recover the same from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: 10. The Claims Tribunal has completely exonerated the insurance company from liability, which is not sustainable in law.

Accordingly, the impugned award is modified to the extent that the insurance company shall first pay the compensation to the claimants and shall thereafter be at liberty to recover the same from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.

11. With regard to enhancement of compensation, this Court finds that the income of the deceased assessed by the Claims Tribunal is on the lower NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:396 4 MA-629-2010 side.

In the considered opinion of this Court, the just and proper monthly income of the deceased, being an unskilled labourer, should be taken as Rs.3,295/- per month as per the Salim Khan vs Smt.Jagjeet Kaur Bagga on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76064929/
2 Minimum Wages Act, instead of Rs.3,000/- per month assessed by the Claims Tribunal.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. As regard to loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700 , the claimants are entitled for loss of income including future prospects.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Pranay Sethi (supra), future prospects be added at 40%.

Further,
as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 , even if age of the deceased is to be taken into account, the appropriate multiplier applicable in the present case is 18.
13.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to receive compensation under the following heads:
 HEAD   Income Rs.3295   Future Prospects@40% Rs.55,35  Dependency 1/2 Rs.27,67  Multiplier 18 Rs.4,98,
 Other Heads:-
 Loss of Consortium Rs.40,00 Loss of Estate and funeral expenses Rs.30,000/-
Total Compensation = Rs.6,08,204/-
14.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation payable in the present case comes to Rs.6,08,204/- as against the sum of Rs.3,08,000/- awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.

Accordingly, the appellant/claimant is held entitled to an additional compensation of Rs.3,00,204/-
over and above the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:396 5 MA-629-2010 amount already awarded by the Tribunal.
15. Consequently, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, and the compensation amount is enhanced by Rs.3,00,204/-.
The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall be paid to the appellants/claimants within a period of three months from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this order.
The remaining conditions imposed by the learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

16. In case the enhanced compensation exceeds the valuation of the appeal, the appellants shall deposit the differential Court fee (if not already paid) within a period of one month from today and furnish proof of such payment before the Registry.
Upon compliance, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of this order.
17. With aforesaid modification, the miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellants stands disposed of accordingly.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *VJ*
